text.content:
Encounters and Evasion

Checklist: switch from 10-minute turns to 10-second rounds; both sides roll 1d6 for surprise (1-2 means surprised); if neither side is surprised both roll 1d6 for initiative, while a surprised side loses initiative automatically; roll reactions if the DM does not already know them; resolve the results; then assume at least one full turn has passed.

Chance of encounter: in a dungeon or city, roll 1d6 every two turns and 1d12 once at night, with an encounter on a 1. In the wilderness, roll 1d6 by day and 1d12 at night: clear, grasslands, inhabited or settled land needs a 1; forest, river, hills, barren land, desert, ocean or aerial needs 1-2; swamp, jungle or mountains needs 1-3.

Surprise: each side rolls 1d6; a 1 or 2 means that side is surprised. If both sides are surprised both lose one round. If one side is surprised, it loses initiative and the other side gains a free round or automatic evasion. If neither is surprised there is no advantage.

Distance: surprise replaces the normal distance with 1d4 x 10 feet or yards; when only one side is surprised it notices at that distance and the surprised side notices at half. Otherwise consult the Encounter Distances Table: dungeon bright light 4d6 x 10 ft, dim light 2d6 x 10 ft, no light 1d4 x 10 ft; wilderness bright 4d6 x 10 yards, dim 2d6 x 10 yards, poor visibility 1d4 x 10 yards; undersea 1d6 x 10 yards.

Monster reactions: roll 2d6 on the Monster Reactions (2d6) table in the BECMI Tables compendium:

2d6Reaction
2-3Monster attacks
4-6Monster is aggressive (growls, threatens); roll again in one round with a penalty of -4 to the roll
7-9Monster is cautious; roll again in one round
10-11Monster is neutral; roll again in one round with a bonus of +4 to the roll
12Monster is friendly

The first roll ignores Charisma. Later rolls apply the speaker's Charisma modifier plus PC actions from a -2 penalty to a +2 bonus and the modifier carried by the previous result. Never roll more than three times; if the third roll is below 10, the monster attacks or leaves.

Evasion and pursuit: an unsurprised group can evade a surprised group automatically. Otherwise the DM rolls d100 against the Evasion Table by party size and number of monsters, adjusted for terrain, relative speed and scouts, with a minimum 5% chance. A failed roll starts a chase: both sides roll 1d6 for initiative each round, and monsters check morale every five rounds.

Settled and castle terrain: a "Castle" result uses Wilderness Subtable 10: Castle Encounters (1d6) in the BECMI Tables compendium. Roll 1d6 for the owner's class, 1d20+8 for level (demihumans have fixed levels), and a second 1d6 for alignment: 1 Chaotic, 2-4 Neutral, 5-6 Lawful. Patrol size and reaction are by class: fighter 2-12 heavy horsemen (pursue on 1-3), magic-user 2-12 heavy footmen (pursue on 1), cleric 2-12 medium horsemen (pursue on 1-2), demihuman 2-12 demihumans (pursue on 1); the remaining results are Ignore or Friendly.

City terrain: a "Special" result uses Wilderness Subtable 11: City Encounters (1d20). First roll 1d8 to select one of its eight sections, then roll 1d20 in that section for the city-dweller; level and intent are for the DM to decide. The same table can be used to pick a location by translating the profession (a judge suggests a courtroom, an undertaker a cemetery).
